feed.title: Ebola Tracker: DR Congo
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: confirmed cases and deaths, affected provinces, spread to other countries, vaccines, WHO risk and a dated timeline.

entry.title: CDC: 10,990 confirmed cases and 5,354 deaths in DR Congo
entry.summary: CDC's situation summary, with data as of 8 November, counts 10,990 confirmed cases and 5,354 confirmed deaths in DR Congo. CDC's counts differ from the DR Congo national health institute's 30 October figures because the agencies use different reporting dates and methods. CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.
entry.content:
CDC's situation summary, with data as of 8 November, counts 10,990 confirmed cases and 5,354 confirmed deaths in DR Congo. CDC's counts differ from the DR Congo national health institute's 30 October figures because the agencies use different reporting dates and methods. CDC calls it the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.

Sources: CDC Ebola situation summary

entry.title: ECDC: 10,741 confirmed cases and 5,230 deaths

entry.title: WHO expert groups recommend two more candidate vaccines for the Tumaini trial
entry.summary: WHO said its independent vaccine advisory group recommended two candidates, ChAdOx1 BDBV and Moderna's mRNA-1469, for further clinical evaluation. They are expected to join the Tumaini trial in DR Congo once national approvals are in place.

entry.title: Kenya releases 46 contacts and discharges five patients
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said 46 contacts completed monitoring without symptoms and were released from quarantine on 3 November, bringing the total released to 66, and that 52 remain, expected out by 11 November. Five patients were discharged after testing negative and two remain under treatment. Kenya's count stays at nine confirmed cases, two of them fatal. The ministry said the outbreak would not be declared over until a 42-day countdown is complete.
entry.content:
Kenya's health ministry said 46 contacts completed monitoring without symptoms and were released from quarantine on 3 November, bringing the total released to 66, and that 52 remain, expected out by 11 November. Five patients were discharged after testing negative and two remain under treatment. Kenya's count stays at nine confirmed cases, two of them fatal. The ministry said the outbreak would not be declared over until a 42-day countdown is complete.

Sources: Kenya News Agency, Washington Times (3 Nov), Xinhua (4 Nov)

entry.title: CDC Ebola attestation requirement takes effect for flights to the US
entry.summary: Under a CDC order signed on 22 October, passengers on international flights to the United States must attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the previous 21 days. The requirement took effect at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November and runs to 18 December unless changed.

entry.title: DR Congo institute: 10,414 cases and 5,372 deaths as of 30 October
entry.summary: A situation report from a DR Congo national health institute counts 10,414 confirmed cases and 5,372 deaths as of 30 October, a case fatality rate of 51.6%. Bloomberg names the National Institute of Public Health and Africanews the National Institute of Biomedical Research. Bloomberg reported that the rate rose above 50% after health authorities "added hundreds of previously unallocated fatalities to the official toll"; Africanews described the increase in deaths as "a retrospective adjustment of data between the local data processing team and the Ituri Province outbreak management team", not a single-day surge. ECDC's latest count, from data up to 28 October, is 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths.

entry.title: Nigeria identifies two suspected cases in the north-east
entry.summary: Nigeria's centre for disease control (NCDC) said on 31 October that it has identified two suspected Ebola cases in the north-east of the country. The two people are in isolation while laboratory tests and contact tracing begin. NCDC said that being classed as suspected does not mean a case is confirmed, and that confirmation depends on laboratory results. Nigeria's one confirmed case remains the imported case reported on 20 October.

Sources: Channels Television (31 Oct), Gazette NG, TBS News

entry.title: Nigeria: two suspected cases test negative
entry.summary: Nigeria's centre for disease control (NCDC) said the two suspected Ebola cases it identified in Adamawa State, in the north-east, tested negative after two rounds of laboratory tests. The agency's director general, Jide Idris, said there is no laboratory-confirmed case in Adamawa and that the imported case confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on 20 October remains Nigeria's only confirmed case.

entry.title: DR Congo deaths pass 5,000, government data show
entry.summary: DR Congo government data show the Ebola death toll has passed 5,000, with more than 10,000 people infected since the outbreak was declared in May, Reuters reported on 30 October. Al Jazeera carried the same milestone on 31 October. ECDC's latest count, from data up to 28 October, is 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths.

Sources: Reuters via Yahoo News (30 Oct), Al Jazeera (31 Oct), ECDC: Ebola disease, multi-country outbreak 2026

entry.title: African health ministers agree to keep borders open
entry.summary: After an extraordinary virtual meeting of African health ministers on 28 October, Africa CDC's director general Jean Kaseya said the ministers agreed to prepare every country, coordinate across borders and keep borders open while watching them closely. He told the meeting the continent is not winning so far, per Anadolu, TRT Afrika and Premium Times.

entry.title: Kenya releases the first 20 Ebola contacts from quarantine
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry released the first 20 contacts after 21 days of monitoring without symptoms. Health Director-General Patrick Amoth said the outbreak is not over; the remaining 98 contacts are expected to leave quarantine in four waves from 3 November, based on individual health assessments, Reuters reported.

entry.summary: Nigeria's health minister approved the evacuation of the patient confirmed on 20 October, who was moved to Switzerland on 26 October. Nigeria's centre for disease control (NCDC) said it was following 54 primary contacts, monitored for 21 days from their last possible exposure.

entry.title: Nurse killed in attack on Ebola responders in Tshopo
entry.summary: A nurse was killed and another health worker seriously injured on 24 October in Bafwasende, Tshopo province, while responding to an Ebola alert, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, as reported by AP and Al Jazeera. WHO condemned the attack.

entry.title: First participant vaccinated in the Tumaini trial
entry.summary: CEPI said the first participant was vaccinated on 23 October in Bunia, DR Congo, marking the start of Tumaini, a pivotal Phase 2/3 trial of vaccine candidates against Bundibugyo virus run with Epicentre, MSF, WHO and Africa CDC. Bloomberg reported that the first dose was Ervebo, which is licensed for the Zaire species; whether it protects against Bundibugyo is not yet known. Experimental candidates from Moderna and from Oxford with the Serum Institute of India could be added within weeks, Bloomberg reported.

entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry announced the death of a patient who had been in quarantine, the second death among Kenya's nine confirmed cases. The ministry said all confirmed cases remain within one cluster of known contacts, with no evidence of community spread, and that the other seven patients are receiving care, AP reported.

entry.title: Africa CDC investigates a possible link between the first Kenya and Nigeria cases
entry.summary: Africa CDC said the first patients confirmed in Kenya and Nigeria both passed through Entebbe airport in Uganda on 3 October, and that whether they crossed paths there is one theory being investigated, AP reported. Kenya's health ministry has said all nine of its cases belong to one cluster; Nigeria has placed 44 contacts under follow-up.

entry.title: CDC requires an Ebola attestation for all US-bound air passengers
entry.summary: CDC issued an order requiring every passenger boarding an international flight to the United States, whatever their nationality, to attest that they have not been in DR Congo in the 21 days before boarding. The requirement starts at 11:59 pm Eastern time on 3 November, and airlines must check the attestation before boarding. It adds to CDC's existing entry restrictions for travellers recently in DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.

Sources: CDC order, NBC News, CNBC Africa (Reuters)

entry.title: Kenya confirms a ninth Ebola case
entry.summary: Kenya's health ministry said one more person tested positive, bringing the total to nine including the first patient, who died. The new case is a contact of the first patient who was already in quarantine. The ministry said all nine cases belong to one cluster, that there is no evidence of transmission outside it, and that 134 of 135 identified contacts were in quarantine. It said the first group of contacts completes 21 days of quarantine on 25 October.

entry.title: Nigeria confirms an imported Ebola case
entry.summary: Nigeria's health ministry confirmed one case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, in a person with recent travel to Uganda; laboratory confirmation was on 20 October. Officials said 44 contacts had been identified. WHO calls it an imported case and the fifth country to detect the virus since the outbreak was declared, says where and when the person was exposed is not yet known, and advises against restrictions on travel or trade.
